_source.description: Major global tellurium production sites (copper smelters/refineries with Te recovery)
_source.origin: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2024 (https://pubs.usgs.gov/periodicals/mcs2024/mcs2024-selenium-tellurium.pdf); USGS Minerals Yearbook — Selenium and Tellurium chapter (https://www.usgs.gov/centers/national-minerals-information-center/selenium-and-tellurium-statistics-and-information); Jinchuan Group Ltd annual reports (https://www.jnmc.com); Jiangxi Copper (SHA: 600362) Annual Report 2023; Tongling Nonferrous Metals (SHA: 000630) Annual Report 2023; Daye Nonferrous Metals (China) annual disclosures; Mitsubishi Materials Corporation (TYO: 5711) Annual Report 2023; Sumitomo Metal Mining (TYO: 5713) Annual Report 2023; Pan Pacific Copper (JV of JX Nippon Mining/Mitsui) disclosures; Teck Resources (TSX: TECK.B / NYSE: TECK) Annual Report 2023; Glencore CCR Montreal corporate disclosures; Boliden AB (STO: BOL) Annual Report 2023; UMMC (Ural Mining and Metallurgical Company) corporate reports; ASARCO LLC (Grupo Mexico subsidiary) public disclosures; Rio Tinto Kennecott (UTH) corporate reports; Umicore (EBR: UMI) Annual Report 2023; PASAR (Philippine Associated Smelting and Refining Corp.) disclosures; Aurubis AG (ETR: NDA) Annual Report 2023; KGHM Polska Miedz (WSE: KGH) Annual Report 2023; Southern Copper Corporation (NYSE: SCCO) disclosures
_source.license: USGS: public domain; company data: fair use summary
_source.notes: Tellurium is almost entirely a byproduct of copper refining, recovered from copper anode slimes during electrolytic refining. Sites listed are copper smelters and refineries that have tellurium recovery circuits. Global production ~580 tonnes/yr (2023). Exact production figures per facility are rarely disclosed; capacity estimates based on USGS data, company reports, and industry analysis. Coordinates from company disclosures, USGS facility records, and satellite verification.

_coverage.global_production_source: USGS MCS 2024 — estimated 580 tonnes refined tellurium (2023)
_coverage.known_gaps: Smaller Chinese copper refineries with undisclosed Te recovery; some Russian and Indian copper smelters with potential Te byproduct recovery

sites.name: Jinchuan Nonferrous Metals (Gansu)
sites.notes: China's largest nickel-copper producer; Te recovered from copper anode slimes; Jinchang city, Gansu Province

sites.name: Guixi Smelter (Jiangxi Copper)
sites.notes: China's largest copper smelter; ~1.5M tpa copper cathode capacity; major Te source; Guixi city, Jiangxi Province

sites.name: Tongling Nonferrous (Jinchang Smelter)
sites.notes: Major Chinese copper smelter; Tongling city, Anhui Province; Jinchang smelter complex

sites.name: Daye Nonferrous Metals
sites.ownership: China Nonferrous Metal Mining Group (CNMC, state-owned)
sites.notes: Daye city, Hubei Province; integrated copper mining and smelting; Te from anode slimes

sites.name: Zijin Copper (Shanghang Smelter)
sites.notes: Shanghang county, Fujian Province; Zijin's flagship copper smelter; Te recovery from electrolytic refining

sites.name: Shandong Yanggu Xiangguang Copper
sites.notes: One of China's top 5 copper smelters by capacity; ~800k tpa copper cathode; Yanggu county, Shandong Province

sites.name: Yantai Penghui Copper (Shandong)
sites.notes: Mid-size Chinese copper refinery with selenium and tellurium byproduct recovery; Yantai, Shandong Province

sites.name: Naoshima Smelter & Refinery
sites.notes: Naoshima island, Kagawa Prefecture; one of Japan's largest copper smelters; ~230k tpa copper; major Se/Te producer

sites.name: Toyo Smelter & Refinery
sites.notes: Niihama, Ehime Prefecture; ~450k tpa copper capacity; Sumitomo Besshi copper tradition since 1691

sites.name: Saganoseki Smelter & Refinery
sites.ownership: JX Nippon Mining & Metals (60%) / Mitsui Mining & Smelting (40%)
sites.notes: Oita Prefecture, Kyushu; Japan's largest copper smelter (~450k tpa copper); Te and Se from precious metals refinery

sites.name: Trail Operations
sites.notes: Trail, British Columbia; world's largest integrated zinc-lead smelting complex; Te from copper residues and specialty metals circuit

sites.name: CCR (Canadian Copper Refinery)
sites.notes: Montreal East, Quebec; ~340k tpa refined copper; tellurium and selenium from anode slimes; precious metals refinery

sites.name: Ronnskar Smelter
sites.notes: Skelleftea, Vasterbotten; one of the world's most efficient e-waste and complex materials recyclers; major European Se/Te source; ~250k tpa copper

sites.name: Uralelectromed (UMMC Verkhnyaya Pyshma)
sites.ownership: UMMC (Ural Mining and Metallurgical Company, private)
sites.notes: Verkhnyaya Pyshma, Sverdlovsk Oblast (near Yekaterinburg); Russia's largest copper refinery; ~380k tpa refined copper; Te from anode slimes

sites.name: Norilsk Nickel (Kola Division)
sites.notes: Monchegorsk, Murmansk Oblast (Kola Peninsula); Te recovered as byproduct from copper electrolysis; part of Nornickel's Kola Division

sites.name: ASARCO Amarillo Copper Refinery
sites.ownership: Grupo Mexico (NYSE: GMEXICO, via ASARCO LLC)
sites.notes: Amarillo, Texas; US's primary tellurium source; ~300k tpa refined copper; processes copper anodes from ASARCO Hayden and Ray smelters in Arizona

sites.name: Kennecott Utah Copper (Rio Tinto)
sites.notes: Bingham Canyon (Magna), Salt Lake County, Utah; integrated mine-smelter-refinery; ~275k tpa copper; Te from precious metals plant

sites.name: Hoboken Plant
sites.type: precious metals refinery / secondary copper with Te recovery
sites.notes: Hoboken, Antwerp; world's largest precious metals recycling facility; processes complex feed materials; Te from copper anode slimes and e-waste

sites.name: PASAR (Isabel Smelter)
sites.notes: Isabel, Leyte; Southeast Asia's only primary copper smelter; ~210k tpa copper; Te recovery from anode slimes processing

sites.name: Hamburg Copper Refinery (Aurubis)
sites.notes: Hamburg-Veddel; Europe's largest copper refinery (~450k tpa copper cathode); Te and Se recovered in precious metals circuit

sites.name: Glogow Copper Smelter/Refinery
sites.ownership: KGHM Polska Miedz SA (WSE: KGH, Polish state 31.8%)
sites.notes: Glogow, Lower Silesia; KGHM's primary smelting complex; processes domestic Legnica-Glogow copper belt concentrates; Te from anode slimes

sites.name: La Caridad Copper Complex
sites.ownership: Southern Copper Corporation (NYSE: SCCO, subsidiary of Grupo Mexico)
sites.notes: Nacozari de Garcia, Sonora; integrated mine-smelter-refinery complex; ~290k tpa copper SX-EW + smelter; Te from anode slimes in refinery

sites.name: First Quantum Kansanshi Smelter (development Te recovery)
sites.notes: Kansanshi mine & smelter, Solwezi, North-Western Province; smelter commissioned 2015; Te recovery circuit under evaluation; currently processes ~300k tpa copper
